newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia lawmaker wounded, election tension rises.
newsitem.headline: Colombia lawmaker wounded, election tension rises.

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper called an emergency meeting of his security council after a car-bomb attack on a senior lawmaker on Monday, officials said.

Julio Enrique Acosta, member of the ruling Liberal Party and vice-chairman of the lower house of Congress, was wounded in the attack by suspected leftist guerrillas at the gates of a cemetery in the northeastern town of Arauca. His bodyguard was killed.
The blast followed threats from guerrilla groups and right-wing paramilitary forces to step up attacks before local government elections in October.

"As a result of this lamentable attack and with a view to guaranteeing the safety of members of Congress and candidates in the forthcoming elections, the president has called an extraordinary meeting of his defence and national security council," the presidential palace said in a statement.
The council, grouping armed forces commanders and government ministers, wqs due to hold the meeting with samper early on Monday evening.
October's elections will be for town mayors and provincial governors. Congressional elections will be held next March followed by a presidential election in May.
Seven guerrillas and two soldiers died in three separate firefights across northern Colombia and in the east of the country on Monday, an army spokesman said.
